en: Vimānavatthu:
The Chapter on the Pāricchattaka Tree in the Section on Female Vimānas
8. The Story of the Mansion of Mallikā “Clad in yellow garments, with a yellow banner,
and adorned with yellow ornaments;”
Adorned with lovely golden armlets,
you shine as if encircled by them.
O wearer of shell-bracelets and golden armbands!
Adorned with golden crests,
covered by nets of gold,
and garlanded with various jewels.
Made of gold and of ruby,
made of pearl and of beryl;
of emerald and together with ruby.
It is variegated with gems having eyes like those of the *pārevata* bird.
Herein, there is the beautiful cry of various peacocks,
and the beautiful cry of the royal swan and the *karavīka*.
Their cry is heard, sweet-toned like a five-fold musical instrument played in harmony;
and your chariot is beautiful and lovely.
Inlaid with various jewels,
it shines, beautifully divided by relics of many colors.
O deity, you who stand upon this chariot of golden-bright hue illuminating this region—
being asked, please explain.
“What is the fruit of what deed?
“A golden net, inlaid with jewels and gold,
studded with pearls and covered with a lattice of gold;”
When Gotama, the immeasurable one, had attained final Nibbāna,
with a mind full of serene confidence, I made an offering to him.
Having performed that deed, I—
It is wholesome and praised by the Buddha;
free from sorrow, happy,
joyful, and free from illness.”
The Mallikā-vimāna is the eighth.
